baseline.approach: Compare goal against every circular offset without constructing rotated copies.

archived.name: Doubled string with strstr
archived.time: O(n) copy plus libc-dependent substring search; O(n^2) under a naive substring-search model, not a C-standard complexity guarantee

why: Doubling expresses rotation as a substring test, but strstr's algorithm is not fixed by C, so the source alone does not prove a better worst-case bound.
quantitative_comparison: The archive allocates 2n+1 characters and makes one substring call. A call count does not quantify that search's internal comparisons; no measured speedup or general space advantage is established.
tradeoffs: Potentially concise code trades for extra storage. Checked allocation failure is returned as false, and strcpy correctness relies on the computed capacity and valid terminated inputs.
evidence_basis: Static formulation/storage comparison, with unknown libc substring implementation; no benchmark.
